reconstructed_application_steps.text: Let C be a complete nontrivially real-valued rank-one field, V=C-degree-zero valuation ring, and choose a in V with0<|a|<1. For every positive epsilon some |a|^n is smaller; hence the a-adic topology on V agrees with its valuation topology. Completeness and separation give V=lim V/a^n. Surjectivity can be checked by coherent representatives whose successive differences lie in a^nV; they are Cauchy, with limits inside V. The transition kernels are nilpotent. V is local, and aV is contained in its maximal ideal. No discrete value group, Noetherian hypothesis, or maximal completeness is required.

Application hypotheses still to be verified for each actual curve construction: a proper a-adic formal V-scheme whose reductions X_n over R_n=V/a^n are flat and finitely presented, together with compatible invertible sheaves M_n. The special fibre X_kappa must be a proper curve and every component degree of M_kappa must be strictly positive. Then33.44.15 supplies fibre ampleness. Spec(V/a) has exactly one prime: for every x in the maximal ideal of V, rank one gives x^r in aV for some r. Apply37.50.3 to X_1→Spec(V/a); its neighbourhood of that unique point is the whole base. Thus M_1 is ample even though this nilradical need not be nilpotent. This avoids replacing the reduced fibre by a falsely Noetherian thickening.

Explicitly repair the Noetherian Serre step in the application of37.10.6. The proper flat finitely presented pair(X_1,M_1) descends to a pair(X_0,M_0) over a finitely generated Z-subalgebra R_0 of R_1. Increase the finite stage to retain flatness and properness and to make M_0 ample, using32.8.7,32.13.1,32.10.3 and32.4.15. Now R_0 is Noetherian. Use30.16.1 to choose d_0 with all higher cohomology of M_0^d zero for d≥d_0. By36.32.4 the corresponding degree-zero pushforward is a finite locally free module and all derived base changes preserve it. In particular this gives the desired vanishing and locally free H0 on X_1 over the possibly non-Noetherian R_1. This is a reconstructed application argument, not an independently reviewed theorem or an assertion that the entire recursively generated descent chain has been read.

For every X_n, properness, flatness and finite presentation make RΓ(X_n,M_n^d) perfect with arbitrary base change. Its reduction to R_1 is a vector bundle in degree zero for d≥d_0. Since R_n→R_1 is nilpotent, this forces the same on R_n. A local elementary justification: represent a perfect complex by bounded finite free modules over the local ring R_n; cancel every invertible differential matrix entry by splitting off a contractible two-term summand. In the remaining minimal complex every differential reduces to zero modulo the maximal ideal. Its residue-field cohomology is concentrated in degree zero, so all free terms in other degrees have rank zero. The surviving term is finite free in degree zero. This argument applies to each d and gives compatibility H0(X_m,M_m^d)⊗R_n≅H0(X_n,M_n^d), not a guessed lifting of independent sections.

Use the truncated algebra A_n=R_n⊕⊕_{d≥d_0}H0(X_n,M_n^d). The complete37.10.6 statement and proof show finite presentation, X_n=Proj A_n, and the crucial M_n=O_Proj(A_n)(1), all compatibly. Its finite-presentation reduction uses a descended Noetherian high-degree section algebra, Artin-Tate, and adjoining only finitely many finite projective lower-degree pieces. The identity with the original line bundle avoids accidentally algebraizing only a tensor power or a different polarization.

Over these local R_n, all compatible finite projective degree modules are finite free of constant rank. Lift a basis at n=1 successively to each n+1; nilpotent Nakayama and equal ranks show each lifted basis is a basis. Their compatible sequences give B_d=lim(A_n)_d≅V^r_d, and B_d⊗R_n≅(A_n)_d. Degreewise compatible multiplication defines B=⊕B_d. This is a direct local proof of the needed part of15.13.4 and does not require V to be Noetherian.

Lift a finite positive-weight homogeneous presentation of A_1 to Ψ:V[T_1,...,T_s]→B. In each degree the target B_d is finite free and Ψ is surjective modulo a; degreewise Nakayama gives surjectivity. Each degree kernel is finite projective, as the surjection to B_d splits. This splitting also makes reduction of the kernel exact, so each finite homogeneous relation F_j downstairs has a homogeneous lift G_j in the kernel. In every degree, the kernel quotient by the ideal generated by the G_j is finite and zero modulo a; Nakayama gives zero. Therefore B is finitely presented. Exactness here uses projectivity of B_d, not merely right exactness of tensor product.

Set X=Proj B and M=O_X(1). The flat degree modules give flat X and M; graded base change recovers all X_n and M_n. Finite presentation makes X proper projective over affine Spec V and M finitely presented. The invertible locus for M contains X_1. Its closed complement has proper closed image in Spec V missing the closed point; every nonempty closed subset of a local spectrum contains that point, so the complement is empty. M is invertible. Apply fibre ampleness37.50.3 at the closed point of Spec V: every open neighbourhood of that point is the whole local spectrum. Thus M is relatively ample and has exactly the compatible reductions originally prescribed.

If the original formal pair has rigid generic fibre already identified with the analytification of the actual smooth projective curve and its given tensor power of L, the proper algebraic pair above has the same formal completion and hence the same generic analytic pair. Fully faithful proper rigid GAGA identifies its generic carrier and line bundle with the original algebraic ones. This final identification is an application obligation: name the actual formal-generic-fibre equivalence and GAGA hypotheses and prove the initial formal pair and line-bundle identifications. No change of ground field or normalization of mass is introduced. Component degree equals raw curvature weight only after the actual slope/degree identification has been proved.

For a prospective atom or graph approximation, use a small positive fraction of an already genuine ample reference model metric to make each component degree strictly positive, while retaining the graph approximation within the prescribed uniform error. Apply F2-F9 to that actual compatible formal line bundle. The limiting metric may be nef with zero component degrees; algebraization is applied to each strictly positive approximant, not asserted directly for the limiting nef formal bundle. Approximation of graph functions, positivity margins, actual global formal Cartier gluing, and equality of the same-bundle metric are separate required proofs.
